why.headline: Practise catching the ball in front of your face.

claims.text: Two young goalkeepers practised goalkeeper skills with video guidance and feedback.
One study taught children to throw and catch from a wall.
Children with a coordination disorder practised once weekly for 4 weeks. One group caught 31% more balls.
The study's gaze-training group practised once weekly for 4 weeks. They caught 51% more balls.

keep_up.text: Everyone learns at their own pace. Young people develop at different rates.

map.plain: The muscles at the front of your upper arms
The muscles at the back of your upper arms

note.text: An adult study measured these muscles in a different one-handed catch.

claims.text: In the children's study, both groups practised a throw and catch task. Their instructions differed.
The study found no clear group difference in simple catch success.

limits.text: The study used a wall rebound, not a parent's toss. It does not predict your result.
The goalkeeper study included only two children. Their practice used video feedback.
